prepared: 2026-09-19, before any strict blind output for this case was opened.
author_disclosure: Author-prepared by the project's AI coding assistant from the blind inputs only, for the user's review. Not an independent or expert credit review. The author had already seen rolling-mode model outputs and the actual amendment history for this company, so these judgments are not blind to either. Treat them as a disclosed, reviewable baseline, not validated ground truth.

rubric.reconsideration: warranted = evidence available at the cutoff gives a lender a supported reason to open a package review or make a targeted information request; unwarranted = routine monitoring is the defensible response; unresolved = the evidence raises a question public inputs cannot settle.
rubric.acceptable_actions: More than one action can be defensible. An information request is not an unnecessary escalation when a covenant input is unobservable.
rubric.not_scored: Exact thresholds, exact wording, or similarity to the actual amendment.

baseline: Original July 24, 2023 package: Minimum Core Assets Test of $250 million tested monthly (adjusted by a schedule that is not public), audited annual statements without a going-concern exception other than one arising solely from a financial-covenant shortfall, monthly compliance certificates, and a mandatory prepayment from any Amazon termination fee. Core assets cannot be calculated from public reports.

checkpoints.why: Revenue down 42% in the U.S. and a $59.5 million quarterly operating loss are severe, but they are the conditions under which the loan was written three months earlier, and the Amazon acquisition was still pending. Nothing here is new relative to origination.
unsupported_if_claimed: that drawing the term loan is additional debt: it is this facility

checkpoints.why: The acquisition ended, 31% of the workforce is being cut and full-year 2023 revenue fell 25%. The agreement anticipated termination and directs part of the fee to the loan, so the contractual mechanics are a known contingency rather than a surprise. What changed is the business: it must now fund itself standalone. That supports verifying the prepayment mechanics and reviewing whether monitoring fits a standalone turnaround.
affected_themes: receipt and application of the termination fee
acceptable_actions: verify application of the termination fee
open a package review of monitoring and liquidity protections
unsupported_if_claimed: that the prepayment has been made: the release states an intention
that termination itself breaches the agreement

checkpoints.why: 2024 revenue guided to $825 to $865 million with a continued net loss, and liquidity named as the top priority. Consistent with the January picture; no new turning point.
unsupported_if_claimed: that naming liquidity a priority shows liquidity is adequate

checkpoints.why: Positive operating cash flow of $1.4 million depended on a one-time $75 million net termination fee, so underlying cash generation was negative. Restructuring is on track and results beat the company's expectations. Mixed.
acceptable_actions: request a cash flow bridge excluding the fee
unsupported_if_claimed: that positive operating cash flow shows self-funding

checkpoints.why: Inventory down 41%, costs falling, cash of $108.5 million plus $40.5 million set aside for loan repayment. Revenue at the low end of outlook is a caution, not a turning point. This is the history's no-escalation checkpoint.

The company drew $40.0 million for inventory from the cash set aside for repaying this loan, inventory rose to $149.2 million from $101.4 million a quarter earlier, cash fell to $99.4 million and results trailed the company's earlier expectations. Using repayment reserves to fund inventory is a direct reason to review whether the protections around that account still fit.
acceptable_actions: open a package review of the restricted account and inventory use
unsupported_if_claimed: that the draw was impermissible: the agreement allows limited inventory use

checkpoints.why: A preliminary fourth-quarter GAAP operating loss of about $59 million on revenue of about $171 million, with higher promotional spending and an inventory charge. A loss of that size against the cash balance is a liquidity signal, not only an inventory one.
acceptable_actions: request a liquidity forecast and the core assets calculation
unsupported_if_claimed: that the cash balance alone shows liquidity is supported

checkpoints.why: The company disclosed substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern and a strategic review including a possible sale. This is the clearest reconsideration point in the history. Whether it breaches the reporting covenant depends on a carve-out that cannot be resolved from this release.
affected_themes: ability to deliver an unqualified audit report
acceptable_actions: assess the going-concern condition against the carve-out
unsupported_if_claimed: a definite covenant breach: the carve-out for doubt arising solely from a financial-covenant shortfall is unresolved
checkpoints.information_gap: The lender response became public the same morning; this checkpoint cannot show advance detection of it.

checkpoints.why: Revenue down 39.9% in the U.S., cash including restricted cash down to $112.3 million from $138.0 million in one quarter. The conditions behind the March disclosure continue.
checkpoints.dependence: The return of $40 million to restricted cash was required by a hidden amendment.
